Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long‑weekend holidays that apply to most of Canada in 2023**.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a public holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday (or is observed on a Monday when the statutory holiday falls on a weekend).  The table shows the date, the holiday name, and the provinces/territories where the holiday is observed.  (If a holiday is observed nationwide, the “Province(s)” column simply says “All”).

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Province(s)/Territory(ies) where it is observed | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|
| **Feb 20** | Family Day | Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | All provinces & territories | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Fri‑Sat‑Sun). |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | All provinces & territories | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |
| **Jul 1** | Canada Day | All provinces & territories | Falls on Saturday → 3‑day weekend (Fri‑Sat‑Sun). |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | All provinces & territories | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | All provinces & territories | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas Day | All provinces & territories | Falls on Monday → 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |

| Province/Territory | Long‑weekend holidays in 2023 |

| **Nunavut** | Good Friday (Apr 7), Victoria Day (May 22), Canada Day (Jul 1), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the list broken down by province only, or if you need additional details such as the exact day of the week for each holiday.
